instructions.content: Use papers' IDs, not titles: the paper subcommand requires a Semantic Scholar paper ID, an arXiv:-prefixed arxiv ID, or a DOI; titles go to search.
Use Semantic Scholar author IDs, not names, with the author subcommand.
Choose the subcommand by goal: search for keywords, paper for full metadata, author for publications and h-index, citations for citing or cited papers.
Set up the environment on first run following references/setup-and-troubleshooting.md.
Give arxiv IDs the arXiv: prefix when passing them as --paper-id.
To find an author ID, run search for the author's papers and read the authorId from the JSON result.
Export any result to JSON with --format json and --output.
Present the candidate list to the user and offer to triage promising papers with triage-paper.
For known papers, pass the arxiv ID or DOI directly to triage-paper step 1.
NEVER pass a paper title to the paper subcommand.
NEVER pass an author name to the author subcommand.
NEVER loop subcommands to exhaustion: without an API key the limit is 100 requests per 5 minutes; batch with a sleep or set SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY.
NEVER treat search ranking as completeness; qualify results as top results by Semantic Scholar relevance ranking.
NEVER auto-triage search results; confirm with the user which papers to triage.
NEVER use a DOI and a Semantic Scholar ID interchangeably without the correct prefix; confirm the ID type.
Prefer this skill over google-scholar-search whenever both are available.
Do not use the script when the semantic-scholar MCP server is configured; optionally prefer the MCP.
Do not use this skill for biomedical papers not covered by Semantic Scholar; consider PubMed.
Do not use this skill for Google Scholar-exclusive sources such as patents and grey literature; use google-scholar-search.
